teams.heading: Ireland name Joey Carbery in XV squad to face Fiji A
teams.body: Joey Carbery is in Mark Sexton's 28-man Ireland XV squad to meet Fiji A in Cork, a second-string side Andy Farrell is using to widen his pool before next year's Rugby World Cup. The 31-year-old out-half has not played for Ireland's senior side since 2022, when he won the last of his 38 caps against Fiji. Sexton said: "This is a hugely important fixture for players to put their hands up and try to break into the senior Men's squad." Charlie O'Shea, the 20-year-old out-half, is left out.

lead.why: The only fresh squad news in the pack, and it puts Fiji A's Cork opponents and a Fiji-capped Irish recall candidate at the centre of the story.

teams.heading: Borthwick turned down Shaun Edwards's offer to work at England's World Cup
teams.body: Shaun Edwards says he told Steve Borthwick he would take any role on England's staff, even "assistant kit man", but the head coach was content with his set-up. Borthwick's defence structure for Australia 2027 is already settled, with Richard Wigglesworth overseeing it alongside Byron McGuigan and Joe El-Abd. Edwards, 60, who left France earlier this year, has instead signed with Argentina until the end of the tournament.

lead.why: A fresh, two-outlet story in which England's head coach turned down a high-profile offer of help for the World Cup set-up.

teams.heading: Nolann Le Garrec's latest hamstring injury lets Paul Graou into France squad
teams.body: La Rochelle's Nolann Le Garrec has suffered another hamstring injury, and Toulouse scrumhalf Paul Graou comes into the squad in his place. It is one of five additions Fabien Galthié has made to his 42-man group, which must first prepare for Fiji and then face the Springboks at the Stade de France. Argentina follow at the same ground.

lead.why: The Le Garrec hamstring injury is a fresh development in the squad story, and the Graou call-up is a late change that the earlier edition did not cover.

teams.heading: Former Ireland cap Brendan Mullin contests perfume theft charge in Dublin court
teams.body: Mullin, accused of stealing Hermès perfume worth €158 from Brown Thomas on Dublin's Grafton Street in May, told Dublin District Court he was pleading not guilty. The 62-year-old, who won 55 Ireland caps between 1984 and 1995, represented himself because of a row with the Minister for Justice over legal aid reforms that has led many solicitors to withdraw from District Court cases. Judge John Hughes set eight March as the hearing date and remanded him on continuing bail.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item with concrete facts that Ireland's edition has not already run, while the Healy and Prendergast stories were covered in earlier editions.

teams.heading: Erasmus restores Salmaan Moerat to Springboks XV for Italy clash
teams.body: South Africa have officially named the side for Saturday's Turin Test, with lock Salmaan Moerat back from the neck and toe injuries that kept him out of the first leg of the Nations Championship. Moerat partners Ruan Nortjé in the second row, and Ethan Hooker is the only player retained from the September loss to Australia. Italy, meanwhile, have 15 key men unavailable through injury, including captain Michele Lamaro and Tommaso Menoncello.

lead.why: South Africa's officially named XV is a fresh selection event for the Italy Test, and it returns Moerat from injury.

teams.heading: Matfield warns All Blacks Scotland could be bigger test than England
teams.body: Speaking on the Rugby Rivals podcast, former Springbok lock Victor Matfield said Scotland might be a bigger challenge than England, pointing to the two URC clubs. He said the Scottish teams are "really playing great and they're playing nice rugby." He noted Glasgow are unbeaten and Edinburgh were unbeaten before their Benetton loss. Former New Zealand wing John Kirwan agreed Scotland would be a serious threat.

lead.why: A fresh pundit verdict on the Murrayfield test that is not a rehash of the squad injury news already run today.

teams.heading: Steff Emanuel shines as Cardiff beat Ospreys 26-0 in Welsh derby
teams.body: Emanuel was the standout in Cardiff's emphatic derby win at St Helen's, the 20-year-old centre credited with helping create three tries, including both of Tom Bowen's and Josh Adams' touchdowns. He also held up Keelan Giles over the line late on to protect the clean sheet, finishing with 15 carries and 17 tackles. Tom Shanklin called the performance "probably perfect", and Jonathan Davies suggested Emanuel could one day be an option for Wales at inside centre if they persist with a playmaker at 12.

lead.why: A fresh, concrete club result with a named young centre whom a former Wales back links to the national 12 jersey, which beats the unconfirmed team prediction and the URC story already reported.

teams.heading: England A name eight Test-capped men for Argentina XV clash in Bath
teams.body: Mark Mapletoft has named a 30-man group for the Argentina XV game at The Rec, with Caluori, Atkinson and Ojomoh among those who attended Steve Borthwick's three-day senior camp last week. Alongside them, Roots, Northmore, Blamire, Kloska and Carpenter make up the eight Test-capped men. Max Hicks, an English-qualified Newcastle Red Bulls forward, is arguably the headline pick, while Fitz Harding captains the side. Five players, Lucas Friday and James Pater among them, earn their first A call-ups.

lead.why: It is the freshest new item in the pack, and it puts the Argentina XV fixture in front of the reader while the Miotti and Prendergast stories have already run.

teams.heading: England rule out Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland for Wallabies Test
teams.body: England's preparations for the Wallabies have been hit hard at scrumhalf, with Northampton's Alex Mitchell facing a scan on a hamstring injury and McParland sidelined by a calf problem sustained at training camp. Steve Borthwick has called up Ben Spencer and Harry Randall to cover, while first-choice fly-half Fin Smith is battling a calf strain and has until Wednesday to prove his fitness. Borthwick says Australia "have played a significant amount of Test rugby in recent months," which makes the Wallabies' visit the sternest test of England's patched-up squad.

lead.why: A fresh, corroborated team-news event (England's scrumhalf and fly-half problems before the Wallabies Test) that is the strongest new item on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Japan's new kick-catch switch now being countered by opponents, note.com analysis says
teams.body: The analysis describes a shift Japan have made this year: on high kicks player B, not player A, takes the catch, which cuts the risk of conceding penalties for escorting but leaves the catcher running backwards with only one team-mate in support. The writer says the method is now being countered, with pressure on the catch or a deeper kick among the options, and that the issue was highlighted in the Fiji match on 24 October, which Japan lost 28-34.

teams.heading: Justin Marshall warns Dave Rennie against a 'revolving door' in northern Tests
teams.body: Marshall, on the GBRANZ podcast: "I don't see them buttoning off at all, I don't see any point of us having a revolving door," he said. New Zealand still face Scotland, Wales and England in the round-robin, plus a fourth match at Twickenham on finals weekend, and Marshall says the tries and bonus points matter because they sit behind South Africa on points differential. Kieran Read believes Rennie is more likely to rotate, though he says the players can handle four Tests in a row.

teams.heading: Erasmus keeps six uncapped Springboks waiting, hopes to give them tour chances
teams.body: Riley Norton, Emmanuel Tshituka, Yaqeen Ahmed, Markus Muller, Sebastian de Klerk and Luan Giliomee are all in the travelling squad but not in the match 23 for Saturday's Test against Italy in Turin. Erasmus says the six have joined camp and will be exposed to the Bok structures this week, with chances to come later on tour. "They are special players, who all bring something different to the team, and we have full faith in their talent and skillsets."

lead.why: A new item on the six uncapped squad players, a different angle from the match 23 story already reported, with a coach quote and named players.
